newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil govt, lawmakers agree civil service reform.
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt, lawmakers agree civil service reform.

text.p: The Brazilian government reached an agreement with disgruntled members of the chamber of deputies over a controversial pay and pensions ceiling included in its civil service reform bill, officials said.

Under the agreement, the lower house will vote on the reform bill itself later Wednesday and next week on an amendment which would soften the blow of the proposed 10,800-reais ($10,188) monthly ceiling on pay and pensions for public sector workers.

Political Affairs Minister Luiz Carlos Santos said all categories of public sector workers including civil servants and lawmakers would be allowed to hold on to one pension of a maximum of 10,800 reais on top of their current salaries, even if that took them over the 10,800 real limit.

The government had previously said it would not back down to pressure from within Congress where many lawmakers, who earn generous pensions from previous public sector posts, stood to lose under the reform.
"No one is going to earn more as a result of this bill. It will remove privileges," Santos said, denying the government had backed down over the ceiling.
"Democracy is a permanent process of trying to reach agreement," he added.

The ceiling is one of the central elements of the reform bill which will also allow states and municipalities to dismiss currently unfireable workers if their payroll spending is equivalent to more than 60 percent of receipts.
Santos said the reform would lead to the saving of eight billion reais a year in public sector spending on pay and pensions, equivalent to over one percent of gross domestic product.
A deputy close to the government who asked not to be identified said the proposal was "a disaster" and hoped public opinion would pressure lawmakers to vote against the amendment next week.
As a constitutional amendment, the bill requires two three-fifths majorities in the Chamber of Deputies and in the Senate.
